```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(jabotR)
```

This guide demonstrates how to use the `jabot_coverage()` function in the `jabotR` package to measure how well a JABOT-hosted herbarium represents the species diversity recognized by the [Flora e Funga do Brasil (FFB)](https://floradobrasil.jbrj.gov.br/consulta/).

## Function Overview

Unlike [`jabot_gaps()`](/articles/identify_jabot_gaps.qmd), which focuses on species that are *missing* from a collection, `jabot_coverage()` characterizes the species that are *represented*. Overall coverage is the number of FFB species held by the herbarium divided by the total number of FFB species, multiplied by 100.

The analysis includes overall FFB species coverage, coverage by taxonomic group/family/phytogeographic domain/Brazilian state, coverage of endemic versus non-endemic species, representation of type material, graphical summaries, and a self-contained HTML report.

This tool is ideal for reporting collection strengths — e.g. for institutional assessments, grant applications, or deciding which taxonomic groups a herbarium already represents well.

## Arguments

| Argument | Description |
|---|---|
| `herbarium` | Herbarium acronym in uppercase (e.g. `"RB"`). |
| `jabot_path` | Path to a directory with previously downloaded JABOT DwC-A files. `NULL` downloads automatically. |
| `format` | Static formats to save individual figures: `"pdf"`, `"png"`, or both. The HTML report is always generated regardless. |
| `fig_width`, `fig_height` | Dimensions (in inches) of saved figures. |
| `open_report` | If `TRUE`, opens the HTML report in the default browser after rendering. |
| `verbose` | If `TRUE`, prints progress messages. |
| `dir` | Output directory. Defaults to `"<herbarium>_representativeness"`. |

## Basic Use Case

```{r}
coverage_analysis <- jabot_coverage(herbarium = "RB",
                                    verbose = TRUE,
                                    open_report = TRUE,
                                    dir = "RB_representativeness")
```

## Exporting Individual Figures

```{r}
coverage_analysis <- jabot_coverage(herbarium = "RB",
                                    format = c("pdf", "png"),
                                    verbose = TRUE,
                                    open_report = TRUE,
                                    dir = "RB_representativeness")
```

## Reusing a Previously Downloaded Dataset

```{r}
coverage_analysis <- jabot_coverage(herbarium = "RB",
                                    jabot_path = "jabot_download",
                                    format = "pdf",
                                    verbose = TRUE,
                                    open_report = TRUE,
                                    dir = "RB_representativeness")
```

## Example Output

The HTML report ranks families by how well they are covered, and maps overall coverage percentage by Brazilian state:

![Best- and worst-covered families in the `jabot_coverage()` HTML report](/figures/jabot_coverage_report_families.png){.lightbox}

![Choropleth map of herbarium coverage by Brazilian state](/figures/jabot_coverage_report_state_map.png){.lightbox}

The function also returns (invisibly) a named list with every computed data frame, so summary numbers can be pulled directly into other analyses:

```{r}
#| eval: false
#| echo: true
coverage_analysis$coverage_pct
coverage_analysis$endemic_coverage_pct
head(coverage_analysis$family_rep)
```

## Tips

- Coverage and gaps are two views of the same comparison — run `jabot_coverage()` alongside [`jabot_gaps()`](/articles/identify_jabot_gaps.qmd) for a complete picture of a herbarium's standing against FFB.
- `endemic_coverage_pct` is often lower than overall coverage; it highlights Brazilian endemics that are especially valuable to prioritize for future collecting.
- Supply `jabot_path` on repeated runs to avoid re-downloading FFB and JABOT data.
